speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned sudden-onset vertigo; can you describe exactly how you started feeling dizzy and if you experienced any hearing loss, tinnitus, or nausea?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)

The brief duration of your symptoms (3 minutes) and the sudden onset while going to bed are classic indicators for BPPV. To confirm this, I need to perform a physical exam; does moving your head quickly cause the spinning sensation again right now?
